q: What carbon data do EU buyers ask Binh Duong furniture makers for?
title: Furniture maker carbon data for EU buyers
short: A footprint per piece or per cubic metre of wood, built from factory electricity and fuel, the wood, board, foam and hardware per piece, and the finishing chemicals. Furniture is not a CBAM good unless declared as steel or aluminium articles, but buyers counting Scope 3 ask for it.
audience: Wooden and upholstered furniture makers in the Binh Duong cluster in Vietnam

ul: Electricity for saws, CNC, dust extraction and spray booths.
Fuel for kiln drying, often wood waste or biomass: record quantities even where biogenic.
Solid wood and board volumes, with species and origin.

p: The EU Deforestation Regulation covers wood and furniture, with traceability to plot of land. Steel furniture declared under a steel heading can fall under CBAM. Keep origin records alongside the carbon data.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
